To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size fractionation of the charcoal layer collected on the ground after a forest wildfire can be used to separate fractions with distinct properties, which are most likely primarily imposed on the charcoal by fuel source and to a lesser extent by burning conditions, and can be used for reconstructing the history of forest fires.
size fractionation of charcoal and ash can be used to separate charcoal of different fuel sources and recalcitrancy, and to select the appropriate number of size fractions for analysis.

(i) particle size fractionation can be used as a tool for studying charcoal in wildfires, (ii) particle size is a useful criterion for separating forest charcoal of different fuel sources, and (iii) the mineral ash content can be used as criterion for selecting an appropriate number of size fractions to analyse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology to improve the use of charcoal as a tool for reconstructing wildfires in terrestrial environments.
the development of an approach to characterise forest wildfire combustion products that is robust and applicable to a wide range of ecosystems and wildfires.
the identification of charcoal as a proxy for fire history in terrestrial ecosystems, and with the development of a methodology for the characterisation of charcoal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
charcoal particles of different size have different properties, but these properties are mainly determined by fuel source rather than burning conditions.
size fractionation can help to better understand the complex nature of the forest wildfire combustion residues.
size fractionation is a powerful technique to study charcoal, provided that the analyst is aware of the underlying processes and the possible limitations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the charcoal size fractionation is a powerful tool to separate the different combustion products and their recalcitrance, which is of paramount importance for reconstructing past wildfires.
size fractionation is a powerful tool for separating the charcoal of different origin and recalcitrant properties in wildfire ash layers.
size fractionation can be used as a tool to isolate the charcoal of different fuel sources and recalcitrances in the wildfire ash/charcoal layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

size fractionation can be a valuable tool to separate the combustion products of wildfires in terms of fuel type and recalcitrant carbon, and thus can be a useful approach for studying the role of wildfires in the carbon cycle and in the formation and evolution of soil organic matter.
the properties of the charcoal fraction of a forest wildfire are strongly influenced by the fuel type, which can be identified and separated from the ash layer by size fractionation.
the charcoal properties are not homogeneous and, therefore, the charcoal in a given layer should be analysed by considering the size fractions.
